record.paper_title: Concrete examples of the rate of convergence of Chernoff approximations: numerical results for the heat semigroup and open questions on them (with appendix: full list of pictures and Python code)
record.original_question: For the heat equation u_t(t,x)=u_xx(t,x) on the real line, work in the Banach space UC_b(R) of bounded uniformly continuous real functions with the sup norm. Let Lf=f'' generate the heat semigroup e^{tL}. For t=1/2, compare the exact solution e^{tL}u0 with Chernoff products G(t/n)^n u0 and S(t/n)^n u0, where G is first-order Chernoff tangent to L and S is second-order Chernoff tangent to L. Write d_n^G=||e^{tL}u0-G(t/n)^n u0|| and d_n^S=||e^{tL}u0-S(t/n)^n u0||, and estimate log d_n approximately as alpha log n plus beta, where alpha is the order of decreasing error and beta is the free term. Why do the sampled errors d_n^G and d_n^S oscillate around their fitted power-law trends as n changes, forming waves rather than lying on a monotone or nearly straight log-log curve? What theoretical feature of the Chernoff products, the heat semigroup, the selected initial conditions, or the finite-n sampling causes this oscillatory error behavior?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $UC_b(\mathbb{R})$ denote the Banach space of bounded uniformly continuous functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ equipped with the sup norm $\|f\|=\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}|f(x)|$. Consider the heat equation $u_t(t,x)=u_{xx}(t,x)$ on $\mathbb{R}$, whose generator $Lf=f''$ produces the strongly continuous heat semigroup $(e^{tL})_{t\ge 0}$ on $UC_b(\mathbb{R})$. Define the bounded linear operators
$$(G(t)f)(x)=\tfrac{1}{2}f(x)+\tfrac{1}{4}f(x+2\sqrt{t})+\tfrac{1}{4}f(x-2\sqrt{t}),$$
$$(S(t)f)(x)=\tfrac{2}{3}f(x)+\tfrac{1}{6}f(x+\sqrt{6t})+\tfrac{1}{6}f(x-\sqrt{6t}).$$
Here $G$ is Chernoff-tangent to $L$ to first order and $S$ to second order, so by Chernoff's theorem, for every $u_0\in UC_b(\mathbb{R})$ and every $t\ge 0$,
$$d_n^G(t):=\|e^{tL}u_0-G(t/n)^n u_0\|\to 0,\qquad d_n^S(t):=\|e^{tL}u_0-S(t/n)^n u_0\|\to 0$$
as $n\to\infty$. Fix $t=1/2$ and a smooth bounded initial datum $u_0$ (e.g.\ $u_0(x)=\sin x$, $\cos x$, $e^{-x^2}$, or similar). For large $n$ one observes numerically that
$$\log d_n^G\approx \alpha_G\log n+\beta_G,\qquad \log d_n^S\approx \alpha_S\log n+\beta_S,$$
but, plotted against $\log n$, the sequences $\log d_n^G$ and $\log d_n^S$ do not lie on these straight lines: they oscillate around the fitted trend in a wave-like manner rather than following a monotone or nearly linear log–log curve.

Provide a rigorous theoretical explanation of this oscillatory behaviour. Specifically, identify which features of the Chernoff products $G(t/n)^n$ and $S(t/n)^n$, of the heat semigroup $e^{tL}$, of the chosen initial conditions, or of the discrete sampling in $n$ are responsible for the periodic-like waves observed in $n\mapsto\log d_n^G$ and $n\mapsto\log d_n^S$ around their power-law trends.
artifact.status_search_result: The oscillation phenomenon was posed as an unexplained numerical observation among a list of open questions on the rate of convergence of Chernoff approximations to the heat semigroup. Subsequent work (e.g., Galkin–Remizov on tangency-order based rates, and a 2024 Israel J. Math. paper on upper/lower estimates of Chernoff convergence rates) refines power-law estimates of the form $d_n=O(n^{-k})$ but does not address the wave-like deviation from those trends. No source located identifies a theoretical mechanism explaining the oscillations, so the question appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Concrete examples of the rate of convergence of Chernoff approximations
status_evidence.snippet: numerical results for the heat semigroup and open questions on them
status_evidence.claim: The oscillatory behavior is posed as an open numerical observation.

status_evidence.title: Upper and lower estimates for rate of convergence in the Chernoff product formula
status_evidence.snippet: convergence can be arbitrarily fast or arbitrarily slow; provides upper estimates under natural assumptions
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses overall power-law rates but not the oscillation around fitted trends.

status_evidence.title: Chernoff's product formula: Semigroup approximations with non-uniform time intervals
status_evidence.snippet: if Chernoff function and semigroup share Taylor polynomial of order k, error decreases at least like 1/n^k
status_evidence.claim: Higher tangency order improves the leading-order rate but does not explain residual oscillations.
